task:
<Ranger>, you have a unique opportunity to enrich your welfare in a short period of time. The thing is that our airfreight business with the neighbouring Faeyan planets is rather well-run now but we don't have pilots with the category Z-45/6a certificate, which gives them the right to drive Shattlon SLK-5 airfreighters. As soon as we get a sample of this certificate, we'll be able to... so called...prepare several copies to administer our government's needs. We don't care if you steal it or get in conformity with the law. Our chief requirement is to have it by <Date> - the Faeyans are scrupulous in this respect, they like everything to be in law and within the agreed period.

Right now they are testing experienced pilots and give out such certificates in the Certificate Centre on the <ToPlanet> planet in the <ToStar> system. If you hurry up and bring such a certificate  - even in your name - to us by <Date>, you can easily expect to get a nice award in the amount of <Money> cr! What do you think of such a mission?
success: Bravo, ranger <Ranger>! Your gumption and excellent results made you <Money> cr richer! Due to you we'll be able establish airfreight flights to the Faeyan systems, which in its turn will foster the trading and general improvement of the relationship between our races! And the most important thing...we'll have much more opportunities to flog dru... Well, the rest of it is none of your business.
loc.1.0:
After winding once around <ToPlanet>, you landed in the outer Centre's hangar. You had to spend a couple of hours on the weapon deactivation, brain steroid checking, registration and necessary documentation preparation. At last they let you into the main hall with the examinational equipment and trainer-simulator. Anit, a trim Faeyan, took your papers, checked them once again and gave you an examination magnet card:

- All right, ranger <Ranger>, now you are an applicant for the category Z-45/6a certificate. I should say, only a few people managed to receive it after the first attempt, and the rules say that you can repeat the exam only in a year. I hope, you realise how responsible this exam is, don't you? I'll take you into details. The testing consists of two parts. The first part is the theory. You choose a test-paper with three items. Every correct answer means {1} score, all together you must get {2} scores minimum out of three. The second part is practical. You will accomplish an examinational flight on a special link-trainer where you'll be able to demonstrate all your airfreighter navigation skills. All the results will be entered up into your examination card.
You can pass the theory in any of these three rooms, - Anit showed the doors to you, - they are vacant now. Loho-Khan, a Gaalian, is examining in the first room, my countryman Dalany Highbrow is in the second one, and Snipeman Hogger, a Human, is in the third room. See me after you pass the theory for the practical testing. Good luck!
loc.2.0: - Really? - the Gaalian's face lost its gloomy expression and he looked in your eyes with some hope. - Then... I have some private request. I... errr... have fallen in love with a beautiful girl, Bugbubba by name, from the Document control department and want to tell her about my feelings. But I don't even know how to approach her - I fear she will misunderstand me and send me to the rightabouts... Please do something to have her make a date with me, and I'll show her what Loho-Khan has in him! But don't tell her I asked you to help me. If you do everything properly, I'll make it worth your while. Deal?
loc.8.0:
A young Gaalian with the state of body close to emaciation sat at the holographic display looking crestfallen. He took his head in the hands wrinkling the skin on the nape, and was murmuring something. When you entered he didn't even look in your direction.
You approached and handed your examination card to him.
- What is it?.. Oh, yes... - the card slipped out of his hands when he made a foozle to take it. In all appearances, he was very upset.
- Are you alright?
- Yes... I mean, no... Ah, I can't endure it any more... - a very little more and you would have had to run to the nearby shop for a sack of handkerchiefs for the slobbering young man but he stringed himself up to check himself.
- I'm sorry, I'm a little bit upset, - the young examiner hawed and at last looked at you through the huge eyeglasses. He gave you a searching look, thought for a second and suddenly asked: - Look, can you help me if I'll explain my problem to you?
loc.14.0:
The room was rather dim, and it took you sometime to notice Hogger in the far corner. He turned out to be a person in ripe years with "I-have-just-eaten-a-whole-cantle-of-Belucian-lemon" face. He was inspecting you for several seconds and made you want to get back home to your mummy. Then he croaked:

- Aha, next looser? Well, the rules are the same for everyone... You hope to pass the exam at the first attempt, don't you? Let me assure you, <clr>not<clrEnd> everyone succeeds in that, - the examiner grinned stressing the word "not".

You were knocked off your pins by such brassy impudence and wanted to quarrel but suddenly your tongue cleaved to the roof of your mouth and you had a bone in your throat. You felt like a guilty schoolboy.

- All the applicants are divided into two groups- <clr>clever<clrEnd> and <clr>greedy<clrEnd>, - the man went on meaningfully, - greedy fail, clever succeed... We'll begin as soon as you are ready.

You were baffled by the old examiner's speech but still decided to start the testing. You tried to nestle in the soft armchair and inserted your card into the machine slot. The device read the information and there appeared the ready state message. That was it, you burnt your bridges and were ready for ordeals.
loc.14.1:
Faeyan Highbrow who was reading dedicated literature, stood up to greet you:

- Hello, ranger <Ranger>. Your ambition for self-development and self-improvement is very commendable. I can tell you feel rather confident, it means you have prepared very well for the testing. I think, eventually only theory can tell if a pilot deserves the certificate or not. Who needs practice?! I have always been a partisan of deep theoretical knowledge! So, choose your test-paper, and we'll know the limits of your abilities!

You tried to nestle in the soft armchair and inserted your card into the machine slot. The device read the information and there appeared the ready state message. That was it, you burnt your bridges and were ready for ordeals.
loc.14.2:
- All right, choose your test-paper... - Half-heartedly Loho-Khan pointed to the examinational trainer. He looked completely flagging and sat silently aside. You could have offered him 100 000 cr and he wouldn't even have moved his finger to help you...

You tried to nestle in the soft armchair and inserted your card into the machine slot. The device read the information and there appeared the ready state message. That was it, you burnt your bridges and were ready for ordeals.
loc.15.0: You left Room №1 and went to the Document control department. After wandering a couple of times in the Centre's multiple corridors, at last you found the room wanted. Approaching the door you heard females' cut and thrust coming from behind it.
loc.47.0:
You simply passed the message to the examiner. He looked at it yearningly and read it several times. He looked happy. Ultimately, you managed to persuade Bugbubba to make a date with him... Rather, with you but this was not important.

- Thank you, ranger! Now I've got a chance! In return I'll give you <clr>the secret code <clrEnd> entering which you can get a correct answer, to be more precise, save your answer on the card as the correct one. Unfortunately, it works only <clr>once<clrEnd>. Let me examine you quickly - and I'll be getting ready for tonight!

After these words the Gaalian fell into a trance - he must have been meditating before the date. You tried to nestle in the soft armchair and inserted your card into the machine slot. The device read the information and there appeared the ready state message. That was it; you burnt your bridges and were ready for ordeals.
loc.52.0:
The local canteen looked rather tolerable, cosy and clean except for the fact that there were no vacant seats.

- Alright, <Ranger>, - Bugbubba said, immediately taking a survey of the situation. - I'll go and find a vacant table and you make the order so far.

Hungry Bugbubba gave the Peleng sitting at the window an evil glance. He realised that the situation was getting out of hand, took his tricks and got out of the canteen asking no questions. Meanwhile, you went to investigate the electronic panel with the menu on the wall.

loc.59.0:
Feeling much better after lunch, Bugbubba lay back, relaxed and started picking her teeth studiously. She gazed into space thinking about some female's stuff.
"It seems to be working! - you were elated. - Now we need to break the bridge..." 
- Listen, Bugbubba, what if we... - suddenly you noticed that Bugbubba was in post lunch trance and showed no reaction. You should awake her urgently otherwise she'll remain like that the rest of the break.
loc.81.0:
It didn't take you long to find Anit and gave your card to him. After the Faeyan studied it, he said:

- You know theory very well, <Ranger>, I think you won't have any problems with practice! Let's go to the airfreighter trainer.

You followed Anit to the Centre's training terminal, where several duplicates of pulpits with all the instruments and control panels were installed.

- Choose any pulpit, <Ranger>, and let's start. So... - Anit paused for a moment. - I suppose, as a professional, you are skilful enough to take off and land with your eyes closed. But such high-class pilots have other challenges too and one of them is to deliver freight and keep his spaceship safe and sound. So your mission now will be the following: let's imagine that you got into some planet's asteroidal belt. You must shoot all the asteroids on your way. Per one move the gun can shift one level up and down or shoot. The gun's current position will be shown on the indicator below. To win you must <clr> shoot down 20<clrEnd> asteroids and  <clr>miss no less then 15<clrEnd>. Recollect your strength, ranger! And good luck!
loc.85.0:
- Ranger <Ranger>, you have passed the category Z-45/6a certificate test successfully. We congratulate you!

They accompanied you to the certificate-issuing department where after 10 minutes of processing and signing, you became a happy owner of a half-transparent bluish paper with a holographic embodiment and your 3D-projectional hologram.

You didn't even try to hide your enjoyment and hurried to your awaiting spaceship. You still must make it and deliver this certificate to <FromPlanet> by <Date>!
loc.87.0:
You leisurely went on the excursion around the Centre trying to figure out how to get that damned certificate. While different variants were coming into your mind, occasionally you came to the inner passage that was guarded by two huge Maloqs. One of them stepped forward and stood on your way.
- Special pass! - he barked. He seemed to be in non-talking mood.
- I have none, but I'm an applicant for the category Z-45/6a certificate and just don't know which way to choose. Could you please...
- Buzz off then, it's not the place to hang around! - the Maloq cut your speech short.
- What if I'll knock your teeth in?! - the guard's tone began to irritate you a little. A quizzical look passed between the Maloqs. - If I knock out just one tooth, I'll choose the first corridor, if two, I'll go to the second one, if three - to the third!
- Ha-ha-ha-ha, you are a humorist! - The bullyboy grew merry imagining the whole process. - I know an easier way.
loc.88.0:
-Your courage is worthy of respect, pilot! In return, I'll give you some info about the examiners though it's forbidden according to the rules. And you decide yourself where to go.
A Gaalian named Loho-Khan is examining in the first room. He became rather skinny and constantly upset lately - I guess, there are some intimate problems. Due to this, the applicants are getting through a lot - he muffs everything, make mistakes himself, on the whole, that's done it.
Highbrow, a Faeyan, is in the second room. Wannabe theorist! He prefers to think rather then to do. Rejects practical skills completely. Though it might be useful for somebody...
And that Human scumbag, Snipeman Hogger, is occupying the third room. "Money fixes everything!" - is his favourite slogan. We run such hoodlums through the guts for taking bribes on Aikharue Meddona! 
This is all I can tell you.

After giving the guard a silent clap on the shoulder (you had to stand on your tiptoes for that), you decided to act immediately.
loc.88.1: You'd rather keep out of trouble and go take the exam. Which room will you choose?
loc.89.0:
You decided that you have more important things to do and easier ways to earn your living instead of getting some unofficial certificate for the Pelengs. With these thoughts you returned to the spaceport.

<clr>Your mission failed.<clrEnd>
loc.93.0:
- What's the problem, pilot? Can I really help you? - the examiner grinned.

- Yes, I need your help, I'll make it worth your while, - you winked cunningly to Hogger.

- Really? - the Human got surprised. - And how far will your gratitude go?
loc.93.1:
- What is it, <Ranger>, a poser? - Snipeman Hogger asked and smiled greedily.

- Well, not a complete poser, - you murmured. - But a good piece of advice wouldn't be redundant.

- Expert advice is not cheap! - the examiner cut it short.
loc.93.2:
- Can I ask you for a second? - you asked the examiner. - I have a question.

- Sure, you can! - Snipeman Hogger was all smiles. - But note that the quality of my answer will be directly proportional to the material support of the question!
loc.93.3:
- Tell me, please, - you called the examiner. - The statement of the problem is not quite clear to me...

Snipeman Hogger was looking at you with complete equanimity. 

- Well, here... - you hawed. - There is nothing about it here... Which answer is right?

The Human gazed at you with a vulture-like smile. He seemed to be expecting something.
loc.110.0:
- Had I been a trifle younger, I'd hit on that chappy big time! - a female's voice said with confidence.
- Did you say "chappy"? Give me a break - he's a real man! - another voice piped.
- Ha-ha, a man! I'll let a gobzaurus eat me, if he has ever asked a girl out on a date... - the first voice was cold.
- He did! - the second one didn't quieten.
- So who was it? You? - one more voice boomed.
- No, not me, unfortunately... If he had done so, do you think I'd mind?
- Oh, gosh, your Loho-Khan should get through some training on a female simulator!!! - the third female burst into laughter, which sounded like a stutter of machine-gun.
- Ha-ha-ha, right you are, - the first one agreed and sniggered.
- Damn fools!!! - cheeped the second female.

You got tired of this gossiping rather quickly and decided to enter the room.
loc.111.0:
The door opened automatically and you saw three females fagging over some reports. One of them was a slim and beautiful Human, stylishly coiffure a la "letz-heffan" and wearing a dark blue costume with steel reflections. The second one turned out to be a modest Gaalian girl in a national yellowish costume meditating over the pile of documents. The third one, a Maloq female, had bright ginger hair, a few pieces of clothing on her body and nothing else outstanding in her appearance but for her size.

"Damn it, who is who?! It would be easier, if I try to guess who Bugbubba is", - you thought raking them. Then you flicked space dust off your costume, made a merry face and entered the room...

- Yes, I need your help, I'll make it worth your while, - you winked cunningly to Hogger.

- Really? - the Human got surprised. - And how far will your gratitude go?
loc.127.2:
- Can I ask you for a second? - you asked the examiner. - I have a question.

- Sure, you can! - Snipeman Hogger was all smiles. - But note that the quality of my answer will be directly proportional to the material support of the question!
loc.127.3:
- Tell me, please, - you called the examiner. - The statement of the problem is not quite clear to me...

Snipeman Hogger was looking at you with complete equanimity. 

- Well, here... - you hawed. - There is nothing about it here... Which answer is right?

The Human gazed at you with a vulture-like smile. He seemed to be expecting something.
loc.131.0:
The following message appeared on the screen:

"This was <clr>the first<clrEnd> error. No more errors allowed!"
loc.131.1:
The following message appeared on the screen:

"<clr>Correct!<clrEnd>"
loc.132.0:
The following message appeared on the screen:

"This was <clr>the second<clrEnd> error. Testing complete".

And the card popped crack out of the slot.

Upset, you got off the simulator and parked your ship in the hanger cursing that planet, the Centre and all its employees. <clr>Mission failed...<clrEnd>
loc.134.0:
- Excellent, <Ranger>!!! - the Faeyan exclaimed. - I knew you would do it! You know the theory so well that I think you deserve to get the certificate right now without wasting your precious time on useless practice. I'll talk to Anit, and he'll give the certificate to you without any practice.

And yes, within an hour you got the desired pilot certificate, inscribed in your name - a half-transparent bluish paper with a holographic embodiment and your 3D-projectional hologram. Half an hour later you were sitting in your spaceship already. You still must make it and deliver this certificate to <FromPlanet> by <Date>!
loc.135.0:
The following message appeared on the screen:

"Correct! <clr>Testing complete successfully <clrEnd>".

Your card came out accurately from the slot and you took it cheerfully.

- Excellent, <Ranger>! Two correct answers out of two! - Highbrow was sincerely happy for you. - I haven't got such a good student for a long time! Actually, you can go and take your practice text right now. But you know, <Ranger>, I personally have always considered theory, not practice, to be the keystone of spaceship navigation. So if you cope with the third item in your test paper, I'll liberate you from the practice test. Do you like my offer?
loc.136.0:
The following message appeared on the screen:

"Incorrect. This is <clr>an error<clrEnd>".

- Heh, <Ranger>, if you only knew how much you've disappointed me! - Highbrow was obviously upset. - And I thought that I met a real competent pilot at last... Anyway, you answered correctly twice. So you've passed the theory but I can't liberate you from the practice!

"Get along with your theory!" - you thought leaving the room.
loc.136.1:
The following message appeared on the screen:

"Correct! <clr> Testing complete successfully <clrEnd>".

The card came out accurately from the slot and you took it cheerfully.

- Well, <Ranger>, you answered correctly twice and passed the theory! - the examiner congratulated you. - Go to Anit to take practice.

"Well begun is half done!" - you were joyful leaving the room.
loc.137.0: "First aim, then shoot! And don't mix up!!!" - this was what your sergeant told you before the first firing drills in the army. Those were the days...
loc.137.1: "This is a good simulator, by the way, very realistic", - you thought looking at the next asteroid appearing on the monitor.
loc.137.2: So, shall we move the gun or shoot?
loc.137.3: Your fingers gripped the trigger like grim death. No pasaran!!! Asteroids won't pass!
loc.137.4: "Show me a fool who will carry valuable freight through an asteroid belt! - you thought. - This practical course has as less to do with the ship navigation practice as their theory!"
loc.137.5: "I'll show you now what is what! - you thought looking at the next asteroid. - What if I let it come closer?"
loc.137.6: "Can the gun get jammed here, I wonder? - you thought. - That would be very realistic indeed!"
loc.137.7: "It's still good that these asteroids don't shoot! - you thought. - I wish these trainer-makers were stuck into the battle with dominators! I bet that would have taught them a lesson! It's not just a toy for kids and scholars..."
loc.137.8: Who is stronger - you or asteroids? Stupid question! Coping with asteroids is a doddle for such an experienced pilot like you!
loc.137.9: You glimpsed at the shot asteroids counter: [p23] shot asteroids, that is, {20-[p23]} are left. Not that much, never say die!
loc.138.0:
After a long fudge about the supernew superbiochemical process in some superbugs' cells, Bugbubba felt completely tired and interrupted you:

- Heh, you must be a rare stodger!!! Give me a break and stop describing this nonsense in clever words... You had better have cleaned somebody's clock!
loc.138.1:
You introduce yourself to Bugbubba as a scholar, to be more correct, ammunition designer. To prove it you cited a new gun's tactical and technical parameters that you saw in one of ranger private promo bulletin. Bugbubba was stunned at how tough you were:

- This is what I call a real scholar! But these fancy pants from the Centre are of different kind...like that drip Loho-Khan or stodgier Highbrow...

It seems like the first stage of the acquaintance is a success. Keep it up!
loc.138.2:
Try as you might to praise Loho-Khan and make a hero out of him, you failed...
- You turn out to lack grip like your friend does! So what are you going to do next, fancy pants?
loc.138.3:
You never had problems with eloquence and started picturing one fight after another and Bugbubba, completely intoxicated, listened open-mouthed and hot-eyed. She didn't even notice that you said "...and pulled to pieces the last Faeyan ship!" instead of "... and pulled to pieces the last dominator ship!". God knows why you did that!

- I'm honoured to get acquainted with such a great fighter like <Ranger>! From now on all our neighbours will respect my family!

You seem to gain some of Bugbubba's respect. Keep it up!
loc.138.4:
You were picturing your fights with dominators in space and on different planets. Bugbubba was listening open-mouthed. However, when you started telling her about the system that you had liberated all alone, she interrupted you rudely:
 
- That's a crock! Do you think I am ignorant of the world?! You can't liberate a system all alone! They show it in stereomovies only. Come on, what do you want?
loc.138.5:
You started from afar telling her that you adored issuing school bulletins in your childhood, asking all passers-by stupid questions, and spying on the neighbours with a camera... The last word-painting masterpiece was about your task to interview the Lady Tuff herself, Head of All-galactic bank but instead of it you started to tease her for the underground depositary secret code. Bugbubba was quite reasonable about it:

-This is what I dislike journalists for - you always poke your nose into other people's business! Though you are excellent company!
loc.138.6: You introduced yourself to Bugbubba as a military journalist. To prove it you told her about a couple of fights you took part in. It sounded rather veracious. You also mentioned casually the names of the most famous generals who you allegedly were on friendly terms with and interviewed not once. Your words achieved their objective: in half an hour the huge Maloq female was looking at you as if you were one meter higher than she was. Don't stop at what has been accomplished, make the next step!
jump.31.text: I'm all ears and will do my best
jump.33.text: It's a doddle, I know what to do!
jump.34.text: No, I'm not an expert in this
jump.35.text: Talk female 2 and mention her name
jump.35.desc: - Such a dunce, I am Bugbubba!!! - you heard the Maloq female's rumbling bass - Who are you to bother me for nothing?
jump.36.text: Talk to female 3 and mention her name
jump.36.desc: - O, o! Where did you hear my name, lover-boy? - a mighty beef about two meters high grinned nicely and rose in front of you. - Who are you, lad?
jump.37.text: Talk to female 1 and mention her name
jump.37.desc: - You are wrong, mister! - and the ginger-head Maloq female half got up from the table intercepting the lamplight. - Who are you?!
jump.69.text: I came to take the exam and I'm pressed for time
jump.102.text: Introduce yourself as a celebrated commodore
jump.103.text: Look through the menu and make the order
jump.121.text: Rise from the table, say thank you to everybody and bow low
jump.121.desc: - Pooh, <Ranger>, how vulgar of you! If you were my husband, I would give you a bash on the bonce! - thank goodness, you're not her husband! This thought made you delirious with delight...
jump.122.desc: - You surprise me, <Ranger>, you're good mannered! - you noticed that Bugbubba was nodding her fine big-eared head in approval.
jump.123.text: Pat your and Bugbubba's belly, and the rest of the comers too
jump.123.desc: - That's an interesting rite! Is it what they do at your home? - Bibuba asked. You mumbled in response.
jump.170.text: Lunch is served! Please start scoffing!
jump.170.desc:
Bugbubba was a regular in that canteen, so she gave the grab that you had just brought a qualified glance:
- Hot dog, <Ranger>, you should be a telepathist! This is my favourite set! Good boy! - Bugbubba looked happy and satisfied as if space grace had poured down upon her.

To impress Bugbubba by your "gargantuan male appetite" you tried to polish off your lunch. The Maloq etiquette required doing something after lunch but you couldn't remember what exactly it was.
jump.171.text: Lunch is served! Please start scoffing!
jump.171.desc:
Bugbubba was a regular in that canteen, so she gave the grab that you had just brought a qualified glance:
- Alright, <Ranger>, it's very nutrition though too much, probably! But I said "To hell with the figure" long ago anyway... - and Bugbubba caressed her floppy belly and started shovelling down the food.

To impress Bugbubba by your "gargantuan male appetite" you tried to polish off your lunch. The Maloq etiquette required doing something after lunch but you couldn't remember what exactly it was.
jump.172.text: Lunch is served! Please start scoffing!
jump.172.desc:
Bugbubba was a regular in that canteen, so she gave the grab that you had just brought a qualified glance:
- <Ranger>, it won't be enough even for a dead Faeyan! - Bugbubba looked upset but started consuming dish after dish nonetheless.

To impress Bugbubba by your "gargantuan male appetite" you tried to polish off your lunch. The Maloq etiquette required doing something after lunch but you couldn't remember what exactly it was.

jump.174.desc:
Bugbubba was a regular in that canteen, so she gave the grab that you had just brought a qualified glance:
- <Ranger>, it will fill my maw but not to a sufficiency. Alright, half a loaf is better than no bread, damn you...

To impress Bugbubba by your "gargantuan male appetite" you tried to polish off your lunch. The Maloq etiquette required doing something after lunch but you couldn't remember what exactly it was.
jump.190.desc:
- I did my best but she refused absolutely from dating you, she even refuses to talk about it - she considers you a drip and a fancy pants, - you reported to Loho-Khan.

- I knew it! Heh, bye-bye, my happiness! - it grieved him to the very heart.
jump.230.desc:
Bugbubba started in her seat as if stung and dotted you one:
- What are you doing?! Are you crazy?! Tut-tut, don't do it again. These slobbers are really too much... So, what was I talking about?
- We were just discussing our new date...
- Really? - Bugbubba tried to remember the beginning of the conversation but failed. - And where did we stop?
- You promised to write down the place and time for me, - you said smiling.
- Give me a piece of paper and I will...

Bugbubba grinned cunningly, scratched something on the paper in uneven hand and gave it back to you.
- Well, ranger <Ranger>, lunch is over, I must get back to work, - the superfemale rose from the table nearly knocking it over.
After wishing her good bye, you hurried to Loho-Khan reading the note.
jump.231.desc:
- Huh? Oh, it's you, <Ranger>! So...so what was I talking about? - Bugbubba rather perplexed, collected herself.
- We were just discussing our new date...

jump.232.text: Wave your hand in front of your eyes
jump.262.desc:
You simply passed the message to the examiner. He looked at it yearningly and read it several times.
- Hurray, ranger, she'll be waiting for me in half an hour!!! - and Loho-Kha danced a new popular dance "Gree-cha-cha" a la Gaalian modern youth.

- Give me your card, I'll pass you on theory! I don't' have time to listen to you, my Bugbubba is waiting, and my tail is not fixed yet!!!

In a couple of minutes you got your card back with the information about your excellent score on ship navigation theory. The elated Gaalian ran out on the date, and there only remained for you to find Anit and pass the practice.
jump.266.text: Knit your brows and bark: "Say away!"
jump.267.text: Screw up your eyes and say between your teeth: "So?"
jump.279.text: Get back to the test-paper and choose the answer
jump.284.desc: - What is it??? Do you think my knowledge is that cheap? Than I can only presume that the correct answer is <clr>not 250 cr<clrEnd>...
jump.285.desc:
- Not enough, I'm afraid! - Snipeman exclaimed and whispered: - Very well, I'll tell you: the answers <clr>220 cr, 250 cr<clrEnd> and <clr>270 cr<clrEnd> have never been correct throughout the history of this exam. So now, choose one of the three remaining answers.

So the variants declined in half. Not bad either!
jump.286.desc:
- You are very bright, <Ranger>, and will distinguish yourself! - the examiner was all smiles. Then he straightened his fashionable violet Vershace jacket (no less than 10000 cr in price!), bent over you with a conspiratorial expression on his face and whispered in your ear: 

- Correct answer is {10*([p21]+21)+30*([p21]=1)} <clr>cr<clrEnd>.
jump.287.desc:
- Ranger <Ranger>, - an evil glimpse flashed in the Human's eyes, - I thought you needed my help... I guess, I misunderstood you.

You realised something was wrong. And now you had to solve the problem yourself.

Yor Bugbubba".

- Here! Have I missed anything?
- Nope, we were just discussing our new date...
- Really? - Bugbubba tried to remember the beginning of the conversation but failed. - And where did we stop?

Bugbubba".

"Well, this will do! - you thought. - Now I'll give it to Loho-Khan!"
jump.331.desc:
"If I mit u wans agan, it's yor funeral, skumbak!!!"

"Too bad... she must be out of spirits today, - you though. - I don't think you should show it to Loho-Khan..."
jump.346.desc:
- Excuse me but I need your help, - you winked at the Faeyan cunningly but he remained completely imperturbable:

- I don't understand what help you are talking about. There is everything you need in the test-paper! This information is quite enough to solve the problem. I can't tell you anything else. I can read it out loud, though, if you are illiterate. Shall I?

- No, thank you! - you refused and the examiner turned his back to you. Well, you'll have to try and cope with it yourself.

jump.391.text: That's all right with me, of course - I lose nothing!
jump.392.text: Get along with your theory, I'd better pass the practice!
jump.406.text: Ask Bugbubba to wine and dine you
jump.406.desc:
- What?! - Bugbubba was shocked. - What do you take me for?! Do you consider Maloq females as stupid as to feed every Tom, Dick and Harry if they introduce themselves as commodores?! Get out of here, knave!!! 

And Bugbubba left towards the Centre's canteen. Well, you failed to impress her. Now you'll have to return to Loho-Khan defeated.
jump.407.text: Ask Bugbubba to wine and dine you
jump.407.desc:
- Will such a noble Maloq female buy a simple lunch for a celebrated commodore who spent all his money on the ship repair after the fight with dominators? - you were affability itself.

- I'll be honoured to buy you the best scoff from our canteen! - Bugbubba tried to keep up with the courteous tone but her foolish giggling spoiled all the impression from her answer. You went to the Centre's canteen. The canteen was organised in a queer way: you paid for the entrance and chose any dishes you wanted for free. The entrance cost {150} cr, and Bugbubba paid for both of you.
jump.408.text: Offer to buy Bugbubba lunch (300 cr)
jump.408.desc:
- It's lunchtime now, shall we have a bite in the local canteen? Will you accept my offer if I buy you lunch?

- Yes, of course, I'm constantly hungry! I love to have <clr>a nourishing meal<clrEnd>, but <clr> don't take big quantities <clrEnd> - they make the belly huge and it deforms all the figure! 

The last phrase was especially funny: "What figure is she talking about?! This is a walking wardrobe!". But then you remembered about your hard mission and minced after Bugbubba who rushed to the Centre's canteen. The canteen was organised in a queer way: you paid for the entrance and chose any dishes you wanted for free. The entrance cost {150} cr, and you paid for both of you.
jump.409.text: Offer Bugbubba to have lunch together (150 cr)
jump.409.desc:
- It's lunchtime now, shall we have a bite in the local canteen? - you offered.

- Why not? - Bugbubba said. - Do I really care who is scoffing nearby?

But she seemed to be flattered. You minced quickly after Bugbubba who rushed to the Centre's canteen. The canteen was organised in a queer way: you paid for the entrance and chose any dishes you wanted for free. The entrance cost {150} cr.
jump.410.text: Introduce yourself as a celebrated commodore
jump.413.text: Ask Bugbubba to wine and dine you
jump.413.desc:
- What?! - Bugbubba was shocked. - Did I get it right, that <Ranger>, a scholar, is requesting a poor Maloq plodder to buy him lunch? What do you take me for?! I know it cold that all scholars roll in money like the Pelengs in the mire! So you must have shucked to me about being a scholar. Get out of here, knave!!!

And Bugbubba left towards the Centre's canteen. Well, you failed to impress her. Now you'll have to return to Loho-Khan defeated.
jump.414.text: Ask Bugbubba to wine and dine you
jump.414.desc:
- I invested all my money in the last project, - you complained. - And can't even afford lunch...

Bugbubba was stared blankly at you catching nothing. It seemed like your hint should have been broader:

- Can I borrow some money from you to buy me lunch in the canteen?

- Learned beggar!!! - Bugbubba burst out laughing and almost knocked out the glasses from the windows. - Oh, yes, I think I can buy you lunch and then my colleagues and me will have something to nicker at! Come on!

You minced quickly after Bugbubba who rushed to the Centre's canteen, which was organised in a queer way: you paid {150} cr for the entrance and chose any dishes you wanted for free. Bugbubba paid for both of you.
jump.415.text: Ask Bugbubba to wine and dine you
jump.415.desc:
- Ha-ha! - Bugbubba grinned. - Not likely! Let your buddy Loho-Khan treat you!

And Bugbubba left towards the Centre's canteen. Well, you failed to impress her. Now you'll have to return to Loho-Khan defeated.
jump.416.text: Ask Bugbubba to wine and dine you
jump.416.desc:
- Pauper journalist?! - Bugbubba got surprised. - It just cant' be! You lied to me, you are anything but a journalist. You are just a pilfer who decided to make good at a poor lonely Maloq female's expense. Get out of here, knave!!!

And Bugbubba left towards the Centre's canteen. Well, you failed to impress her. Now you'll have to return to Loho-Khan defeated.
jump.417.text: Ask Bugbubba to wine and dine you
jump.417.desc:
- You know...I got robbed! - you complained to Bugbubba. - I turned an honest penny and everything is now gone: three tape recorders, three stereocameras, and my wallet with cash and documents... Three wallets... Right there in the spaceport. Can you imagine that?! I can't even afford lunch now. Can you help me? And I promise to write an article about you later...

- Yes, of course! - Bugbubba was obviously sympathetic. - If only you know how I hate this thief scum! They are worse than pirates, bless me, the latter can fight at least... And what will be the article about? 

- We'll talk about it later, - you were civil and entrained her gently to the Centre's canteen. The canteen was organised in a queer way: you paid {150} for the entrance and chose any dishes you wanted for free. Bugbubba kept her promise and paid for both of you.
